claims.text: Melt-spinning Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 at approximately 10^5–10^6 K/s yields an amorphous ribbon.
Slow cooling at approximately 52 K/s produces a complex, multiphase crystalline microstructure in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The crystalline products formed during slower cooling include several primary non-eutectic phases.
The melt-spun amorphous alloy is susceptible to crystallization during subsequent reheating.
Conventional reheating produces extensive primary crystallization in the alloy.
Relevant crystallization events during reheating occur over approximately 1120–1300 K.
The uncoated alloy exhibits distinct exothermic crystallization peaks around 1126–1300 K.
A reheating rate of approximately 10 °C/min normally permits primary crystallization in the 1120–1300 K interval.
An ALD-deposited Al2O3 coating applied after melt-spinning will suppress heterogeneous nucleation during later thermal treatment.
The coating inhibits surface and near-surface nucleation sites that promote primary crystalline phases.
The ceramic coating acts as a physical barrier that reduces surface atomic mobility.
The ceramic coating minimizes impurity- or defect-induced nucleation during thermal excursions.
Reduced surface mobility and nucleation will slow the atomic rearrangements required for crystallization.
Coated specimens will retain more amorphous material than uncoated specimens.
Coated specimens will exhibit a higher crystallization-onset temperature during DSC reheating.
Coated specimens will exhibit a reduced DSC crystallization-exotherm area.
Phosphorus and high mixing entropy enhance glass formation during very rapid cooling of this alloy.

contradictions.description: The coating is applied only after the ribbon has already been formed by ultra-rapid cooling, yet the hypothesis also claims suppression of primary crystallization under slower cooling. The cited slow-cooling behavior concerns solidification from the melt, which a post-solidification coating cannot affect unless a subsequent remelting and resolidification step is specified.
